name: Shakti back-and-forth: hippocampal signal left, then right
origin: Todd Murphy (Shakti software), after Persinger's vectorial hemisphericity theory
summary: Murphy's 'interhemispheric intrusion' (back-and-forth) session: 30 min of the hippocampal 'LTP' signal over the left temporal lobe, its 'usually wrong' side, then 30 min over the right. Murphy says the first phase is expected to be unpleasant and the second pleasant.
setting: Advanced users only, after a side test has shown the usual pattern for the signal (this file assumes the usual sides). The vendor says darkness and silence (sensory deprivation) help; eyes closed, relaxed. Run murphy-shakti-test-session-hippocampus first.
schedule: Vendor rules: never on consecutive days, at most every 72 hours or weekly; 60-minute sessions at most once in 3 weeks.
notes: Murphy bases the design on Persinger's vectorial hemisphericity idea: stimulating a structure's negative counterpart first mutes the positive one, and stimulating the positive one next gives what he calls a 'sudden burst'. Murphy links the left hippocampus with irritability and verbal thought and the right with calm and imagery, mostly from user reports; the left/right rule rests on a small Persinger-lab study (Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994: LTP-pattern fields over the right hemisphere were rated more pleasant than over the left). Phase 1 is meant to be unpleasant (the vendor: 'EXPECTED to be unpleasant') and phase 2 pleasant; if phase 1 feels good instead, the vendor reads that as a possible 'reversed' or 'left-handed' structure. The vendor 'strongly' suggests running this procedure with each signal separately (murphy-shakti-back-and-forth-amygdala and -hippocampus) before trying the two-signal option (murphy-shakti-back-and-forth-both). If phase 1 becomes too uncomfortable, press Skip at once to start phase 2, but never stop after phase 1 without phase 2 (the vendor: 'Do NOT apply the signal over the wrong side without following it with the same signal over the correct side'). For unwanted effects that linger, the vendor's undo procedures are the hippocampal signal over both frontal lobes or the ERP signal over the cerebellum (in this project: murphy-shakti-cerebellum-erp). Coils: a cross of four over each temporal lobe (FT7, C5, TP7, T9 and FT8, C6, TP8, T10); each phase drives the four coils of one side together, without movement or channel alternation (none is described for this procedure). The vendor's Alternative procedures page says to apply the signal 'over the (usually) WRONG side of your head for 30 minutes, and then immediately apply the same wave form to the (usually) CORRECT side', without a length for the second phase; its 30 min here is an inference (it matches the first phase and the 30 + 30 min the page gives for the two-signal option; the Bliss page gives 20-30 min per phase). The hippocampal 'LTP' file is proprietary; it is approximated by a point table in the vendor's standard scheme (3-ms points, about 4 s of latency): four theta bursts, each of four biphasic pulses 9 ms apart (after the 4-pulse bursts of Larson & Lynch 1986), one burst every 186 ms (5.4 Hz, the spectral peak the vendor reports for its LTP signal). The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% with hippocampal signals; if so, lower the intensity by one third. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy, seizure history or a psychiatric condition. If phase 1 is distressing, skip to phase 2 as the vendor advises; stop the session if distress continues in phase 2. Revised after a re-check of the procedures page (2026): the length of phase 2 is now marked as an inference, and the page's advice on order and on 'reversed' structures is added; sites, signals and timing are unchanged and remain approximations as described.
